The office was buzzing with the chaotic energy of "Bring Your Pet to Work Day." Dave, a mid-level accountant known for his quiet demeanor and even quieter phone calls, had made a fatal error in judgment. He had brought in Barnaby, a African Grey Parrot with a vocabulary that exceeded his own and a memory like a steel trap.

Barnaby was perched on Dave’s shoulder, preening his feathers while Dave tried to look busy at his desk. The trouble started when Dave’s boss, Mr. Henderson, walked by.

"Hey Dave, how's the merger going?" Henderson asked.

Dave, trying to be professional, whispered into his phone, "No, tell the board the Q3 projections are... let's say, creatively adjusted."

Barnaby tilted his head. "Creatively adjusted," he squawked, loud enough for the entire open-plan office to hear.

Dave froze. "Shh, Barnaby," he hissed.

But Barnaby was just warming up. As Dave’s phone rang again, he stepped into the hallway to take the call, thinking he was safe. "Yes, this is Dave. We’re moving the assets to the Cayman account," he whispered urgently.

From the office, a chorus of squawks erupted. "Cayman account! Cayman account!" Barnaby shrieked, flapping his wings.

Dave sprinted back to his desk, grabbing a stack of files to wave in front of the bird. "Bad bird! No secrets!"

Mr. Henderson appeared, holding a coffee mug, looking suspicious. "Dave, why is your parrot yelling about offshore accounts? And why does he keep saying 'The CEO is a penguin'?"

Dave’s face went pale. "He... he’s been watching too much nature documentaries!"

Barnaby, sensing the tension, decided to add his two cents. "The CEO is a penguin! The CEO is a penguin! Also, Dave, you forgot to file your expense report for the hamster wheel!"

The office fell silent. Dave looked at Henderson. Henderson looked at the parrot. Barnaby looked at Dave, then slowly, deliberately, began to mimic the sound of a cash register. *Cha-ching. Cha-ching.*
